places.name: Observatory
places.intro: The copper dome opens over Starry Bodies. Pull up the sky for today, follow a planet across a map, or step inside a story.

places.name: Field Station
places.intro: Start at the shoreline. These maps follow water, minerals, electricity, and the people making decisions about them.

places.name: Workshop
places.intro: Tools I wanted badly enough to build. Some live in a browser, some work alongside a writer, and a few are still on my workbench.

places.name: Amphitheatre
places.intro: The island after dark. Headphones are handy for the midnight set, recorded down the road at Entelechy.

places.name: Glasshouse
places.intro: Tea for a room full of dancers, an altar you can visit from home, and a small forest made of family stories.

places.name: Reading Room
places.intro: A shelf for essays, field guides, little illustrated books, and one long-running experiment in alchemy by meme.

projects.title: Starry Bodies
projects.summary: Lay today’s sky over your natal chart, follow your planetary lines across a map, or put the whole family in one synastry wheel.
projects.alt: Apollo and Selene beneath the constellations of Starry Bodies.

projects.title: Symbiocene · GAIA AI
projects.summary: Shawn Anderson, Darren Zal, and I build tools for reading landscapes. Four interactive studies follow water from Sacramento farms to the shorelines of the Salish Sea.
projects.alt: An aerial view from the Gowanus stormwater simulation.

projects.title: Cosmic Conference
projects.summary: On Halloween we turned Entelechy on Salt Spring into a conference for interdimensional visitors. The program, delegate badges, photo album, and midnight set live on.
projects.alt: The glass pavilion and glowing landscape of Cosmic Conference.

projects.title: Reword
projects.summary: Give Reword a few pieces you love writing. It learns what makes them yours and brings that voice to a letter, a post, or the next draft.
projects.alt: Reword’s light interface, monospaced wordmark, and electric-lime cursor.

projects.title: Overshoot
projects.summary: Where did the copper in a wire come from? Follow a material through mines, ports, factories, and waste streams. The atlas keeps the sources and gaps in view.
projects.alt: A luminous globe from the Overshoot atlas.

projects.title: White Tara Tea & Botanicals
projects.summary: Mackenzie and I make tea and botanical extracts on Salt Spring. Our online tea house takes the form of an altar with incense, a prayer wheel, and objects you can pick up.
projects.alt: The illuminated White Tara altar with bottles and offerings.

projects.title: Sun Rose
projects.summary: I make bass music as Sun Rose. My midnight set from Cosmic Conference moves from ceremony into the sweatier end of a Salt Spring dance floor.
projects.alt: Sun Rose’s figure surrounded by cosmic fire.

projects.title: Refinery Atlas
projects.summary: At Refinery I worked on where to put the machines. The Atlas helps you look for industrial buildings with existing power for data centres or container batteries.
related: The GPUs Showed Up. The Power Didn’t.
projects.alt: Modular infrastructure at sunset in the Refinery site film.

projects.title: Symbai Studios
projects.summary: My studio builds software with people who know their field. The work ranges from a first working prototype to a private client portal and a workshop for the team using it.
projects.alt: An illuminated sprig growing from a glass seed in the Symbai idea garden.

projects.title: Symbiocene Provider Graph
projects.summary: Choose a place and a restoration job. A branching 3D graph shows how a request could find an environmental service provider.

projects.title: Gaia Ecological Intelligence Layer
projects.summary: An Okanagan research map brings vegetation, water, and drought indicators together. Each layer carries its sources and a record of what has been validated.

projects.title: NOOG
projects.summary: Replace the parts of a feed you didn’t come for with cats, nature, or a little quiet. The image checks run on your device, and you can reveal what they cover.
projects.alt: NOOG’s lime-green site with a cat in the preview.

projects.title: Institute for Terrestrial Integration
projects.summary: Our fictional field office for interdimensional residents at Cosmic Conference. Delegates revisited the 1983 Earth User Manual and submitted revisions for life on this planet.
projects.alt: The Institute for Terrestrial Integration’s field-office interface.

projects.title: The Eternal Wedding
projects.summary: The storytelling side of Starry Bodies. The Eternal Wedding is a myth you can listen to, told through the characters of the sky.

projects.title: María
projects.summary: A browser chapel for Mary, Tonantzin, and Guadalupe. Walk between the three devotional spaces, light a votive, or leave a rose.
projects.alt: Roses and candlelight in the María chapel.

projects.title: Things That Took More Water
projects.summary: I made a picture book about the water cost of using AI. Everyday comparisons lead back to the calculations, sources, and assumptions.
projects.alt: Artwork from the illustrated book on water use.

projects.title: Body Made of Stars
projects.summary: My letters on astrology, mythology, and what the sky stirs up down here. The Phoenix is one of the recent dark-moon essays.

projects.title: Family Forest
projects.summary: An explorable family tree I’m building. Children can wander through an ancestor’s story, while an elder can take a simpler route to the same person.

projects.title: Hunnywomb
projects.summary: I worked with Mackenzie on a digital home for her birth work, Mama Psychedelia, and the women and families who gather around it.

projects.title: Sacred/Saucy
projects.summary: Our home for Salt Spring gatherings, from the first invitation through the sound system and the last dance. The archive includes flyers, photos, and films.

projects.title: Moonbeat
projects.summary: A night of bass music at Mateada. The poster and event archive sit alongside our other island gatherings.

projects.title: Mateada Host Circle
projects.summary: A place for island hosts to bring workshops, performances, and gatherings to Mateada and find out what it takes to put an event on.

projects.title: Unfurl
projects.summary: Paris and I built a system for researching trading strategies, setting exposure limits, and reviewing execution. The public introduction explains how those pieces fit together.
projects.alt: The sculpted botanical wings of Unfurl.

projects.title: Treasury
projects.summary: A household finance app I’ve been building to put accounts, transfers, and a shared view of spending in one place.

projects.title: Riot Act
projects.summary: Benjamin and I have been building a production desk for creative work. It keeps source material, treatments, and the queue of pieces to make in one place.

projects.title: gAIas
projects.summary: A home for people building with AI. The directory and nightly digest make it easier to find a collaborator or catch up with the community.

projects.title: GHG Calculator
projects.summary: A calculation engine with agent tools for emissions factors, units, activity records, and reports. Each result keeps a reference to the factor behind it.

projects.title: Alchememes
projects.summary: An ongoing collection of memes about inner life, internet culture, and the strange overlap between them. There’s a daily edition and an archive to fall into.

projects.title: The Gaian Times
projects.summary: A publication following people and projects working on planetary regeneration. Its editorial process pairs AI curation with human editing.

projects.title: Encyclopedia of Regeneration
projects.summary: A reference work for looking up regenerative ideas and practices across disciplines, built as part of GAIA AI.
